subject: Latin alphabet
hook: LATIN ALPHABET IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The modern 26-letter Latin alphabet is a relatively recent invention, as the letter 'W' was not added until the Middle Ages, and the distinct letters 'J' and 'U' were only separated from 'I' and 'V' during the Early Modern era.
angle_support: It was not until the Middle Ages that the letter ⟨W⟩ (originally a ligature of two ⟨V⟩s) was added to the Latin alphabet
only after the Renaissance did the convention of treating ⟨I⟩ and ⟨U⟩ as vowels, and ⟨J⟩ and ⟨V⟩ as consonants, become established. Prior to that they were allographs.
title: The Latin Alphabet Isn't Ancient
description: We assume the 26-letter alphabet is timeless, but it underwent major changes well after the classical era. The letters W, J, and U were historical additions or late-stage refinements.
narration: LATIN ALPHABET IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture the 26-letter standard as an ancient, rigid relic. It was closer to a work-in-progress, evolving significantly long after the Roman Empire had already fallen away. The letter W was only added during the Middle Ages to accommodate Germanic sounds. Furthermore, the letters J and U were not distinct from I and V until the Early Modern era, functioning only as stylistic variations. Our modern alphabet is a surprisingly recent invention, still settling down.
